Best archaeology museums in India and what to see in them

By @archaeologywala for Talaash Heritage · Updated 15 October 2026

India's best archaeology museums include the National Museum in New Delhi, the Indian Museum in Kolkata, the Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Vastu Sangrahalaya in Mumbai, the Government Museum in Chennai and Patna's Bihar Museum, along with ASI site museums at Sarnath, Sanchi, Nalanda and elsewhere that show finds beside the sites they came from.

Talaash Heritage runs museum gallery studies and object identification labs led by archaeologists, for schools, families and colleges.

Big museums and site museums: two kinds of archaeology collection

India's archaeology museums fall into two broad groups. National and state museums in large cities hold collections from across the subcontinent, often built up since the 19th century, and let you follow Indian history from the Stone Age to the colonial period in one building.

Site museums, many run by the Archaeological Survey of India, sit beside excavated sites and display what was found there. They are usually small, but they connect objects to the ground they came from, which is how archaeologists think. The ASI runs a large number of site museums; our guide to the Archaeological Survey of India explains its role.

Major city museums for archaeology

These museums have the deepest archaeological collections. Check each museum's website for current opening days and galleries before you go, as galleries are sometimes closed for redisplay.

National Museum, New Delhi

For most visitors in north India, the National Museum is the place to start. Its Harappan gallery holds the famous bronze figure from Mohenjo-daro, seals, pottery, beads and ornaments, and the sculpture galleries move through Mauryan, Shunga, Kushana and Gupta art to medieval temple sculpture. There are also strong collections of coins, Central Asian antiquities and Buddhist relics.

The museum is large, so a focused visit works better than trying to see everything. A museum gallery study with an archaeologist takes a group through a few galleries in depth, showing how to read an object's material, style and context.

Indian Museum, Kolkata and Government Museum, Chennai

The Indian Museum, founded by the Asiatic Society in 1814, is the oldest museum in India. Its archaeology galleries include the reconstructed railing and gateway from the Bharhut stupa, one of the key monuments of early Indian sculpture, as well as major Gandhara and coin collections.

The Government Museum in Chennai, one of the oldest in the country, holds sculptures from Amaravati, the great Buddhist stupa site in Andhra Pradesh, and a celebrated collection of South Indian bronzes, many of the Chola period.

Site museums worth the trip

Several ASI site museums hold objects of national importance.

  • Sarnath Museum: the Ashokan lion capital that is India's national emblem, and fine Gupta Buddha images.
  • Sanchi Museum: finds from the stupas and monasteries, including a lion capital from an Ashokan pillar.
  • Nalanda Museum: sculpture, seals and other finds from the monastic site.
  • Lothal and Kalibangan museums: Harappan objects shown beside the sites where they were excavated.
  • Hampi museum at Kamalapura: sculpture and finds from the Vijayanagara capital.
  • Archaeological Museum, Red Fort, Delhi: objects connected with the Mughal court and the city's later history.

How to get more out of an archaeology museum

Before your visit, pick one or two questions: how did Harappan seals work, how did Buddhist sculpture change between Mathura and Sarnath? Then look closely at a few objects rather than glancing at many. Read the label for findspot and date, and ask what material and technique tell you.

Handling replicas first helps a great deal, especially for small objects such as coins and seals. Our museum object identification lab and introduction to numismatics with replicas prepare groups to recognise what they will see in the cases.

Questions people ask

Which is the oldest museum in India?

The Indian Museum in Kolkata, founded by the Asiatic Society in 1814, is the oldest museum in India. It holds important archaeological collections including the Bharhut stupa railing and gateway, Gandhara sculpture and a large coin collection.

Where can I see Harappan artefacts in India?

The National Museum in New Delhi has the largest Harappan gallery in India, including the bronze figure from Mohenjo-daro. Harappan objects can also be seen at the Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Vastu Sangrahalaya in Mumbai and at ASI site museums such as those at Lothal and Kalibangan.

Where is the original Ashoka lion capital kept?

The original lion capital of the Ashokan pillar at Sarnath, adopted as India's national emblem, is displayed in the Archaeological Museum at Sarnath near Varanasi, run by the Archaeological Survey of India.

What is a site museum?

A site museum is a museum built at or next to an archaeological site to display objects excavated there. India's Archaeological Survey runs a large number of site museums at places such as Sarnath, Sanchi, Nalanda, Hampi and Lothal. They let visitors see finds alongside the monuments and excavations they came from.

Are archaeology museums good for school trips?

Yes, especially with preparation. A short session before the visit on what to look for, and a focused route through two or three galleries, works far better than an unguided walk. Hands-on activities with replica objects help younger students connect with what they see in the cases.
